summary: Long-poll fallback delivers out-of-order terminal block after NGINX buffering
description:
Issue summary: NoteFlow (enterprise) reports that when streaming falls back to long-poll behind a CDN + NGINX origin configured with proxy buffering (X-Accel-Buffering), the final terminal block is sometimes delivered out-of-order or duplicated and the finalization metadata is not observed by the client. Impact: UI remains in 'generating' state and server-side snapshot/commit logic never receives end marker, blocking user workflows.

Environment: prod traffic through CDN terminating TLS and proxying to NGINX origin with proxy_buffering enabled. Repro region: us-east-1.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Configure NoteFlow to use SSE streaming with long-poll fallback. 2) Start a long generation (200+ tokens) on redwood/gptx-13b. 3) Introduce a short TCP connection drop between client and CDN midstream to trigger fallback. 4) Observe sequence of chunks delivered via long-poll and whether finalization metadata arrives.

Observed behavior: final content sometimes contains a duplicated trailing fragment (short sentence or ellipsis repeated) and the client does not receive the end/complete metadata. Origin logs show a single final chunk and end event; edge traces show a late coalesced flush that combines prior tail and final bytes.

Expected behavior: fallback must preserve chunk boundaries and deliver finalization metadata exactly once.
logs: 2026-03-12T15:22:11Z origin: choice_id=abc123 seq=1 chunk='The model begins and yields an introduction...'
edge-nginx-trace: flush@15:22:25.120 includes seq=11 tail + seq=12 final; client received coalesced bytes at 15:22:25.121
comments: 2026-03-12 Priya Desai: Initial customer report. Provided request id=abc123 and client trace headers. Customer blocked for commit flow.
2026-03-12 Support: Acknowledged. Setting priority P1 and assigning to infra on-call.
2026-03-12 Marco Alvarez (SRE): Collected proxy and origin chunk traces. NGINX flush timing suggests buffering coalesced small frames into a late flush. Attaching proxy trace.
2026-03-13 Marco Alvarez: Reproduced in staging by enabling proxy_buffering and reducing proxy_buffer sizes; observed duplicate tail fragment on long-poll fallback in ~24% of runs.
2026-03-13 Engineering: Proposed mitigation - set proxy_buffering off for streaming endpoints or ensure origin emits explicit end control event and forces flush prior to closing/resuming transports.
2026-03-13 Support: Customer applied proxy_buffering off as a temporary mitigation; two test runs showed no duplicate fragments. Customer will validate further.
investigation_notes: Origin emits single final chunk and emits explicit end event. No duplicate entries in origin logs.
NGINX origin (with proxy_buffering on) coalesces multiple small writes into a single late flush; the edge->client byte stream contains combined tail+final in one delivery.

Client fallback reassembly expects distinct boundary-delimited frames. When coalesced bytes arrive the SDK heuristics treat the suffix as both a resume fragment and a new final fragment, causing duplication and missing metadata events.
Reproduced locally by running NGINX with proxy_buffering on and small proxy_buffers; intermittent reproduction rate observed.
Related tickets indicate other proxy-induced boundary issues; linking for context.
hypothesis: NGINX proxy_buffering/X-Accel-Buffering coalesces SSE frames; long-poll fallback reassembly is byte-bound and misinterprets coalesced bytes causing duplicated trailing fragments and suppressed finalization metadata.
next_steps: Create minimal integration test: small NGINX with proxy_buffering enabled to validate chunk boundary preservation across SSE->long-poll fallback.
Server-side: emit explicit 'END' control event and force flush before closing/resuming transport (TCP_CORK/TCP_QUICKACK techniques as appropriate).
Client SDK: make reassembly resilient to coalesced frames by deduping trailing fragments by choice_id and treating finalization metadata as authoritative. Add regression tests.
Coordinate with NoteFlow: keep proxy_buffering off for streaming endpoints as short-term mitigation while fixes are developed.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied by customer (proxy_buffering off). Engineering to implement explicit end-marker flush server-side and client-side de-dup in next minor release. Rollout plan: canary server change in us-east scheduled 2026-03-18; client SDK release 2026-03-19. Customer notified and will validate post-release.
